proposal.hypothesis: Giving every eligible training user equal expected pairwise loss mass will improve within-user validation ranking, especially for short and medium histories, and will add marginal portfolio value by reducing the incumbent's exposure-frequency bias.
proposal.implementation_plan: Retain the parent's globally offset categorical feature matrix, but replace the delegated training loop with a self-contained FM BPR loop that samples an eligible user uniformly, then samples one long_view-positive and one long_view-negative exposure for that user. Each sampled user therefore contributes equal expected pair mass regardless of history length. The target block will return train-only long_view labels plus the corresponding train user IDs after DV.assert_trainable. The train block will construct positive/negative row lists per user, optimize the FM score difference with softplus(-(z_pos-z_neg)), and use the current k=32, lr=0.0005, l2=1e-6 and three-epoch budget. The predict block will score the unchanged Xs[split] matrix from the learned linear and embedding parameters. Include a deterministic one-step sign check and a uniform-row-weight parity fixture before the scored user-balanced run.
proposal.justification: The current delegated sampler is optimized over exposure pairs, so prolific users can dominate gradient mass even though evaluation aggregates ranking quality by user. Uniform user sampling directly aligns optimization mass with the evaluation unit and targets the two history slices where the latest ordering regressed.
proposal.observation: Both trusted metrics rank within user, while train histories are highly unequal; the supplied cutpoints for "train_user_history_quartile" are [16,35,64], and the last candidate had negative slice deltas of -0.0003552387347491859 for histories 17-35 and -0.00038142376887939644 for histories 36-64.
proposal.research_nonuse_reason: The supplied BPR evidence concerns ordinary same-user negative sampling, whereas this experiment specifically tests equal expected gradient mass per user; the metric definition and history-slice diagnostics are the more direct basis.
risk: A custom FM loop may not reproduce the optimized stable backend exactly.

proposal.implementation_plan: In build_target, create a local copy of OP_CONFIG with objective="bpr" and call SO.build_target with it. In train, use the same local objective and set the evidence-backed BPR recipe k=16, lr=0.001 and n_neg=1 while retaining l2=1e-6, epochs=3 and batch=8192; remove aux_weight from the local hp dictionary because pure BPR has no censored-watch auxiliary consumer. Delegate to SO.train so its vectorized same-user positive/negative blocks and fixed train-only checkpoint policy remain active. No inference features or prediction logic change.
proposal.justification: The supplied evidence directly supports the complete same-user BPR implementation pattern and its gradient invariants. Reproducing that bounded recipe under the current trusted evaluator tests whether the censored-watch auxiliary is now unnecessary and may yield an error-diverse reward branch for the active portfolio.
proposal.observation: The parent uses objective="bpr_censored_watch", k=32, lr=0.0005, n_neg=4 and aux_weight=0.1, whereas E001 reports that vectorized same-user BPR with k=16, lr=0.001 and one negative improved the official FM over pointwise training. The exact rejected transition in E003 was only aux_weight 0.1 to 0.2 on bpr_censored_watch, not replacement by pure BPR.

research_evidence.query: Which ranking objective and sampling implementation reliably improves the official FM?
research_evidence.reason: Cold-start runs repeatedly proposed BPR but implementation quality varied sharply.
research_evidence.summary: Use vectorized same-user BPR, not all-batch quadratic pairing. Build per-user positive blocks and negative pools only for users with both classes; use one sampled same-user negative per positive per epoch; align positive and negative arrays by user block; return safely when no eligible pairs; the FM global bias cancels. The exact loss is L=mean(softplus(-(z_pos-z_neg))). With diff=z_pos-z_neg, use g_pos=(sigmoid(diff)-1)/pair_count and g_neg=-g_pos. At diff=0, g_pos must equal -0.5/pair_count, never +0.5/pair_count; a one-step sanity check must increase z_pos-z_neg. At k=16, lr=0.001, one negative, the five-seed official-validation primary changed from 0.601500738 ± 0.000481897 for pointwise FM to 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR. Treat the mechanism and implementation invariants as the prior; rerun it inside the Agent harness rather than assuming the measured delta transfers exactly.

selection_rationale: Candidate 0 is the only viable candidate. It proposes a structural, residual-targeted member refinement rather than scalar tuning: uniform eligible-user sampling directly addresses the diagnosed regressions in the 17–35 and 36–64 history slices and aligns training mass with the within-user evaluation unit. The change is connected to executable consumers across target, train, and predict blocks, with explicit train-only label validation, gradient-sign and sampling-parity checks, and unchanged inference features. Its custom FM loop carries implementation and runtime risk, but the experiment contract makes the hypothesis falsifiable and isolates user-balanced pair sampling while holding features and key hyperparameters fixed. No exact matching negative result is supplied, and there are no other viable candidates offering greater expected reliable marginal portfolio gain or information value.
